how_it_behaves: Django admin opens on a centered Log in form. Pressing Enter after typing the password does not reliably submit it, so the blue Log in button below the Password field must be clicked. After a successful login a browser 'Save password?' popup may appear on the right side of the Site administration page and must be dismissed with 'Not now' before clicking anything underneath it. The Site administration home page groups models under headings; Customers is a row under the SHOP heading. The Customers page is a scrolling table headed NAME, EMAIL and CITY with a search box and Search button above it that filters the rows.

skills.name: log_in
skills.does: Log in to Django administration with the given credentials and land on the Site administration home page.

the Password text box, directly below the 'Password:' label in the centered login form, above the blue Log in button
the blue 'Log in' button centered below the Password box in the login form

skills.does: Filter the Customers list by the given customer name and read that customer's email and city, confirming the row name matches.

inputs.customer_name: the customer's full name, e.g. first name then last name

steps.question: Is a browser 'Save password?' popup open on the right side of the screen?
steps.target: the light-blue 'Not now' button in the 'Save password?' popup on the right side of the screen, to the left of the blue 'Save' button

fields.name: the value in the NAME column of the first data row of the customers table, the blue linked name text in that row, not any name in the left sidebar
fields.email: the value in the EMAIL column of that same first data row, on the same horizontal line as the name, not an email from any other row above or below
fields.city: the value in the CITY column of that same first data row, on the same horizontal line as the name and email, at the right of the table

skills.name: lookup_customer
skills.does: Log in, open the Customers list, and report the named customer's email and city.

inputs.customer_name: the customer's full name, e.g. first name then last name

steps.question: Is the customers table still showing a row whose NAME matches the searched customer, with EMAIL and CITY values on the same row?
steps.why: Read the result back at the end so a wrong-row read is caught before reporting the email and city.
